subject: Caution: Change in output structure for ``leave-one-out'' predictive measures

messages.author: 059504e415ddf983
messages.subject: Caution: Change in output structure for ``leave-one-out'' predictive measures
parts:
This is just a post to inform that the structure of the "inla()"-output object has slightly changed
with regards to leave-one-out predictive measures in the newest testing-version.

If the resulting inla-object is `result' and ‘cpo’=‘TRUE’ is specified in ‘control.compute’ (within the "inla()"-call),
the results are now stored as:

results$cpo$cpo         # conditional predictive ordinate (CPO)
results$cpo$pit          # probability integral transform (PIT)
results$cpo$failure     # vector indicating whether some assumptions are violated

see http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-How-can-I-compute-cross-validation-

Hi Andrea,
Can I just check exactly what inla.cpo is computing?  Is it the raw Pr(y_i | y_{-i}) or is it scaled in some way?  I computed the CPO for a dataset where one portion of the data was very very wrong, and it showed up in the CPO plot as a column of large CPO values, which surprised me.  Under the model, these should've been outliers / points with high leverage, so I would've thought that they'd have low CPO values.  The maximum value also appears to be 1.0, which suggests to me that it's been scaled?

Is this true, or am I mis-reading my plot?

Thanks

Dan

messages.author: 059504e415ddf983
messages.subject: Re: Caution: Change in output structure for ``leave-one-out'' predictive measures
parts:
Hi Dan,

ideally inla.cpo recomputes all CPO values for which result$cpo$failure > 0. That means it runs the usual inla-model stored in "result", say, and then checks for failures. For each idx with "result$cpo$failure[idx] > 0" inla is called again using the control.expert = list(cpo.manual = TRUE, cpo.idx = idx) option. Then, I assume that the idx-th observation is internally removed and the cpo-value is calculated from the marginal of linear predictor. To the best of my knowledge there is no scaling involved.

I tried the inla.cpo function out at two examples and also got always CPO values of 1 returned. Thus, I compared it with a "real" manual re-computation, where I remove the observation myself, run INLA and derive the CPO from the corresponding marginal of the linear predictor. Now, I get the expected low CPO values, see the code below. I am not sure what is going wrong in inla.cpo, but I will try to find it out.

Regards
Andrea

########################################################
library(INLA)

data(Germany)
## just make a duplicated column
Germany = cbind(Germany,region.struct=Germany$region)

g = system.file("demodata/germany.graph", package="INLA")

##Define the model
formula <- Y ~ f(region.struct, model="besag",graph.file=g) +
               f(region, model="iid") + x

## Run the model
result <- inla(formula,family="poisson",data=Germany,E=E,
    control.compute = list(cpo=TRUE))

## Find the position of failures
idx.failure <- which(result$cpo$failure > 0)

## Examplary, re-calculate the cpo for one of the failures
i <- idx.failure[3]
## Remove the observation for which we received the failure
y_tmp <- Germany$Y[i]
Germany$Y[i] <- NA

## Run INLA and return the marginals for the linear predictor
result2 <- inla(formula,family="poisson", data=Germany,E=E,
            control.inla = list(int.strategy = "grid", diff.logdens = 5),
            control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE))

## Set back the observation
Germany$Y[i] <- y_tmp
## Get the marginal for the linear predictor
eta.marginal <- result2$marginals.linear.predictor[[i]]
cpo.manual <- inla.emarginal(function(x, yy, EE) dpois(yy, lambda = EE*exp(x)),
                  eta.marginal, yy=Germany$Y[i], EE=Germany$E[i])

## Compare it with the result you get when using the internal option
## to calculate CPO's manually
result3 <- inla(formula,family="poisson", data=Germany,E=E,
        control.inla = list(int.strategy = "grid", diff.logdens = 5),
        control.expert=list(cpo.manual=TRUE, cpo.idx=i),
        control.mode=list(result=result, restart=TRUE))
cpo.inla.manual <- result3$cpo$cpo[i]

## Compare the different CPOs:
## standard INLA (with failure[i] > 0), manual re-computation, inla re-computation)
c(result$cpo$cpo[i], cpo.manual, cpo.inla.manual)
[1] 0.03567603 0.03488637 1.00000000
